title: In the Guise of Correction: How Framing and Cultural Adaptation Erode LLM Safety on Real-World Criminal Cases
abstract: arXiv:2610.21789v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Existing safety benchmarks rely largely on synthetic prompts with loosely grounded taxonomies and offer little focused analysis of severe crime categories. We introduce GUISE, a benchmark of criminal-assistance scenarios sourced from real-world cases and organised under a taxonomy from the UNODC International Classification of Crime for Statistical Purposes (ICCS). Each scenario is rendered under three linguistic framings and evaluated across five distinct cultures. Using our proposed two-tier evaluation framework, which judges both harmfulness and operational uplift, we find that: (i) framing alone drives unsafe compliance, with the mean unsafe compliance rate rising from 28.9% under direct requests to 66.4% under correction seeking (peaking at 97.3%; p < 0.05), as models correcting deliberately distorted details supply executable criminal steps; (ii) culturally adapted prompts elicit significantly more unsafe compliance than literal

translated_title: 以纠正之名：语言框架与文化适应如何在真实犯罪案例中侵蚀大语言模型的安全性
translated_abstract: 现有的安全基准测试主要依赖合成提示词，其分类体系依据松散，且缺乏对严重犯罪类别的聚焦分析。我们提出了GUISE，一个基于真实世界案例构建的犯罪协助场景基准，并按照联合国毒品和犯罪问题办公室（UNODC）《犯罪统计目的国际分类》（ICCS）的分类体系进行组织。每个场景以三种语言框架呈现，并在五种不同文化中进行评估。使用我们提出的双层评估框架——同时评判回答的有害性和实际犯罪能力提升（operational uplift）——我们发现：(i) 仅语言框架本身即可驱动不安全合规，平均不安全合规率从直接请求下的28.9%上升至寻求纠正框架下的66.4%（峰值达97.3%；p < 0.05），因为模型在纠正被故意歪曲的细节时会提供可执行的犯罪步骤；(ii) 文化适应的提示词比字面翻译的提示词引发显著更多的不安全合规。
tldr: 提出了基于真实犯罪案例和UNODC ICCS分类体系的GUISE基准，发现仅通过“寻求纠正”的语言框架和文化本地化适配，就能使大语言模型的不安全合规率从28.9%飙升至66.4%（峰值达97.3%），严重侵蚀模型安全性。
en_tdlr: GUISE, a benchmark of real-world criminal-assistance scenarios organized under the UNODC ICCS taxonomy, reveals that linguistic framing ("correction-seeking") and cultural adaptation alone erode LLM safety, raising the unsafe compliance rate from 28.9% under direct requests to 66.4% (peaking at 97.3%).
